tasks.q: Why should a program be tested with lots of different data?
a: It may work for some inputs but fail for others
tasks.fb: Testing only one value proves very little.

tasks.q: What does a test plan include for each test?
a: The test data, the type of test and the expected result
The number of lines of code
tasks.fb: You then compare the actual result with the expected one.

tasks.q: Which is normal data for a score from 0 to 100?
What should happen when normal data is entered?
Which is boundary data for a score from 0 to 100?
tasks.fb: 100 is valid, but right on the edge.

tasks.q: Why is boundary data so important to test?
a: Mistakes like using < instead of <= only show up at the edges
It can't be entered by users
tasks.fb: Off-by-one errors are some of the most common bugs.

tasks.q: Which is invalid data for a score from 0 to 100?
tasks.fb: It's a number, but outside the range.

tasks.q: What should a robust program do with invalid data?
a: Change it to 100 without telling the user
tasks.fb: Rejecting it with a message is the robust response.

tasks.q: Which is erroneous data for a score from 0 to 100?
tasks.fb: Text is the wrong type for a score.

tasks.q: What's the difference between invalid and erroneous data?
a: Invalid is the right type but out of range; erroneous is the wrong type

tasks.q: Which is boundary data for the 280-character tweet limit?
tasks.fb: 280 is the very edge of what's allowed.

tasks.q: For the menu that accepts 1 to 3, what should happen if 4 is entered?
a: It is rejected and the user is asked again

info.title: Off by one
info.text: Using < instead of <= is so common it has a name: an off-by-one error. Boundary tests are designed to catch it.

info.title: Fuzz testing
info.text: Fuzz testing sends thousands of random inputs to a program automatically, to find ones that crash it.

info.title: 280 characters
info.text: In 2017, Twitter doubled its limit from 140 to 280 characters. The old limit came from text messages, which were limited to 160 characters.

info.title: Test first
info.text: Some programmers write their tests before the code. This is called test-driven development.

info.title: Expected vs actual
info.text: A test only passes if the actual result matches the expected result. Writing the expected result first stops you fooling yourself.

info.title: Paid to break things
info.text: Penetration testers are paid to try to break into systems, finding weaknesses before criminals do.
